sources: Default polygon rasterization updates pixels whose center is within polygon; ALL_TOUCHED is separate.
ALL_TOUCHED includes every pixel touched by polygon geometry.
GDAL documents polygon-center touching behavior as unspecified in the ALL_TOUCHED description.
ALL_TOUCHED output may depend on input feature order at touching edges.
With touching features the last/topmost feature determines edge burn value.
Invert burns outside provided polygon rather than inside.
Nested polygon inversion requires GEOS for correct island-in-lake behavior.
Add mode accumulates rather than replacing pixel values and is unsuitable for a binary terminal membership mask.
Init values do not automatically become nodata metadata.
Target-aligned-pixels aligns output extent to integer multiples of resolution.
Raster and vector optimization modes are documented to produce identical results.
On-the-fly vector reprojection to raster CRS is supported, so terminal provenance must pin whether reprojection occurred.
a_srs overrides output projection metadata and does not reproject features.
Modern gdal vector rasterize exposes explicit all-touched and invert options.
Modern rasterize defaults to Float64 output unless an Int64 field drives output type.
ALL_TOUCHED feature order can affect results in the modern CLI as well.
Target resolution and target size are mutually exclusive output-grid definitions.
GDAL C API describes default polygon rule as center-within rather than all touched.
GDAL C API explicitly says behavior is unspecified when polygon merely touches pixel center.
MERGE_ALG defaults to REPLACE and ADD is an explicit alternate.
Rasterization transformer maps geometry coordinates into destination pixel/line coordinates.
Python RasterizeOptions exposes allTouched=False by default.
Python RasterizeOptions exposes inverse=False independently of allTouched.
Python RasterizeOptions can pin output bounds, width/height or x/y resolution.
Python targetAlignedPixels can force output bounds to resolution multiples.
initValues preinitialize pixels but do not mark those values as nodata.
geometry_mask default includes polygon pixels by center rule, with Bresenham behavior for lines.
geometry_mask default polarity returns False for pixels overlapping shapes.
geometry_mask invert=True reverses mask selection polarity.
geometry_window computes outermost pixel window using floor offsets and ceiling width/height.
geometry_window is a bounding prefilter and does not itself define exact polygon membership.
rasterize default merge algorithm is replace.
rasterize supports add as a separate merge algorithm.
rasterize fill controls pixels not covered by input geometries.
rasterize default_value is distinct from fill.
rasterize transform explicitly maps raster pixels to shape coordinate system.
rasterize skip_invalid defaults True and may skip invalid or empty shapes with warnings.
rasterize raises if no valid shapes remain.
mask all_touched defaults False and uses center rule for polygons.
mask invert=False masks pixels outside shapes.
mask with filled=False returns a MaskedArray where invalid pixels are True in the mask.
crop=True with nonoverlapping shapes raises ValueError.
pad=True expands crop by half a pixel and must not silently change terminal membership.
contains requires no point of B in exterior and at least one interior point of B in interior of A.
A geometry does not contain its boundary under contains semantics.
Polygon contains a strictly interior point but not a point on its boundary.
A point on the boundary of a polygon hole is not contained by the polygon.
contains_xy provides point-in-geometry contains semantics directly from x/y without Point construction.
contains_xy is suitable for replaying many pixel-center coordinates against one prepared polygon.
covers returns True when no point of candidate geometry lies outside the container.
Unlike contains, covers includes a polygon boundary point.
covered_by is the inverse relation of covers.
A point on polygon boundary can be covered_by that polygon.
intersects is true whenever geometries share any portion of space, including touching.
Intersects is broader than center-in-polygon membership and corresponds more closely to touch/overlap diagnostics.
intersection returns the shared geometry between inputs.
Nonzero grid_size snaps inputs/results to a precision grid and therefore must not be introduced silently.
Output resolution and extent must be explicitly controlled when creating a rasterized mask.
geometry_mask requires explicit out_shape and affine transform, enabling exact native-grid parity checks.
Rasterio rasterize can produce a masked result when requested; membership and nodata remain distinct concepts.
contains is not equivalent to covers at polygon boundaries.
ALL_TOUCHED versus center-rule semantics are materially different and must be recorded in provenance.
Crop/window mechanics are separate from the exact per-pixel inclusion rule.
